newsitem.title: UK: New sugar freight orders cited but fixtures few.
newsitem.headline: New sugar freight orders cited but fixtures few.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a number of new orders on Wednesday but reported firmer business was stil thin on the ground, shipbrokers said.
E D & F Man added Dubai as a destination option to its recent order for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Coatzacoalcos/Veracruz to Colombo for January/February.
Sugar Exporters issued a replacement order for 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Recife to Lagos for the end of January.
Glencore quoted for 10/12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to Indonesia for February/March shipment.
The only fixture reported came from Mauritius Sugar Syndicate, which covered 18,500 tonnes min/max bulk sugar on its normal run from Port Louis to London for 4/8 February.
The rate reported was close to stg 16.00, an improvement on the stg 15.00 achieved for the last similar fixture, shipbrokers said.

In Colombia, talks aimed at ending a week-old dockworkers' strike in the Pacific port of Buenaventura ended in a deadlock early on Wednesday. Buenaventura is the shipping point for all of Colombia's sugar exports and is estimated to be losing $500,000 for every day it remains closed.
